metadata.title: ORCHID-Hulls: binary convex hulls (Materials Project, OQMD, assessed CALPHAD)
metadata.description:
ORCHID-Hulls: binary convex hulls (Materials Project, OQMD, assessed CALPHAD): binary formation-energy convex hulls from two DFT databases and isotherms of assessed CALPHAD descriptions, stored as ordered composition intervals (interval schema v1) so energy and the equilibrium phase set at any composition are a lookup. Part of the ORCHID data release v2026.10. Short name in the paper: Hulls.

What

  • hulls/dft-mp/: Materials Project release 2026.04.13 (GGA/GGA+U with the MP2020 compatibility corrections applied by the Materials Project; no further correction added), 3,828 binary systems of 88 elements, 12,829 hull vertices; above-hull entries within 0.05 eV/atom.
  • hulls/dft-oqmd/: OQMD qmdb_v1_8_022026 (fit-partial elemental references applied by OQMD), 3,916 systems, 15,314 vertices.
  • hulls/calphad-sgte/: 2,695 assessed SGTE binary descriptions (1,223 systems) at 298.15 K, same interval schema, solution phases included.
  • Per layer: catalog.json (provenance, summary, per-system SHA-256), elements.json, entries; Parquet table hull_vertices.

How

Deterministic lower-hull builder (standard library, open-tdb) over pinned snapshots; collinear and degenerate structures are retained, upstream stability disagreement is enumerated rather than reconciled; 3,827 of 3,828 MP systems reproduce the upstream stability flag exactly. Agreement in a hull consistency check tests the stated computational representation, not the experimental accuracy of the energies.

Limitations

  • DFT hulls are at 0 K and carry formation enthalpy only.
  • Materials Project and OQMD use different reference states and corrections; their energies are not comparable and must not be averaged.
  • The MP, OQMD and assessed hulls retain their respective database versions, energy conventions and temperatures; comparisons across them require explicit reference-state treatment.
  • OQMD stability is derived by the builder (no upstream cross-check).

Licence

ORCHID's data are released under CC BY 4.0, as are the SGTE (B. Hallstedt, Calphad 89 (2025) 102833), Materials Project and OQMD data from which they are derived; attributions and statements of changes are in NOTICE.md, the licence of each folder in LICENSES.md (both in the bundle).

The stated licence covers the ORCHID-produced content in this deposit; upstream data and software retain their documented terms and attribution requirements, and no publisher pages, handbook drawings or restricted TDB source files are included.

Files: one zip (orchid-hulls-v2026.10.zip) holding the files at their repository paths, a MANIFEST.sha256, the README, CHANGELOG and licence files. Its file list with sizes and SHA-256 is zenodo/hulls.files.json in the data repository.

Software and data citations

These credits describe the ORCHID project and its examples. Cite the papers and software used in your analysis, together with the ORCHID release and original source of each observation. The list does not imply that every dataset was generated with every package. Preserve the versions and commit hashes recorded by each example; a repository link is not a reproducibility pin. Materials Project and OQMD energies retain separate references.

  • pycalphad: Thermodynamic calculations and phase equilibria. R. Otis and Z.-K. Liu (2017), pycalphad: CALPHAD-based Computational Thermodynamics in Python (10.5334/jors.140). Repository.
  • ESPEI: Thermodynamic parameter fitting and uncertainty quantification. B. Bocklund et al. (2019), ESPEI for efficient thermodynamic database development, modification, and uncertainty quantification: application to Cu–Mg (10.1557/mrc.2019.59). Repository.
  • PhaseForge: MLIP-informed CALPHAD construction in the examples. S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Machine learning potentials for alloys: a detailed workflow to predict phase diagrams and benchmark accuracy (10.1038/s41524-025-01814-z). Repository; archived software.
  • PhaseForge+: Construction and experimental tuning of CALPHAD models in the examples; repository name PhaseForgePlus. C. Kunselman, S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Construction and Tuning of CALPHAD Models Using Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and Experimental Data: A Case Study of the Pt–W System (10.1007/s11669-025-01222-2). Repository; archived software.
  • Materials Project: DFT structures and energies; repository link is the API client, not the database itself. A. Jain et al. (2013), Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation (10.1063/1.4812323). Repository; data resource.
  • OQMD: DFT structures and energies; qmpy is the supporting software. J. E. Saal et al. (2013), Materials Design and Discovery with High-Throughput Density Functional Theory: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD) (10.1007/s11837-013-0755-4); S. Kirklin et al. (2015), The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD): assessing the accuracy of DFT formation energies (10.1038/npjcompumats.2015.10). Repository; data resource.
